reports.title: Khalid Yousef: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: The L&D police custody suite model has not commissioned psychiatrists
concerns.hazard: lack of psychiatrists in police custody suites

concerns.quote: Liaison and clarity is needed between Chief Constables and the Trusts providing L&D services on who has responsibility for mentally unwell persons in custody
concerns.hazard: responsibility ambiguity for mentally unwell persons in custody

concerns.quote: West Midlands Police officers and BSMHFT staff do not sufficiently understand the role and limitations of the L&D police custody suite model
concerns.hazard: misunderstanding of L&D role and limitations

concerns.quote: BSMHFT have not learnt sufficient lessons from the incident and need to review experience, training and supervision of L&D practitioners
concerns.hazard: inadequate review of training and supervision

reports.title: Miles Hurley: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

promises.quote: The practice of arresting officers risk assessments being formally completed prior to arrival at custody is inconsistent across forces. Best practice is being considered through the NPCC Betterment Workstream to include a nationally recognised pre arrival risk assessment in place to communicate risks and concerns that may have been raised.
promises.summary: Implement nationally recognised pre-arrival risk assessments to improve communication of risks and concerns

promises.quote: It is recognised that there is a lack of information being recorded on custody detention logs. The College of Policing Hydra packages are in place to improve this and the NPCC are supportive of this training for custody staff. I understand that Sussex Police have now adopted this training.
promises.summary: Adopt College of Policing Hydra packages to improve documentation on custody detention logs

promises.quote: Guidelines around supporting a LDS Practitioner as to when it is appropriate to undertake a formal mental health assessment when an individual is intoxicated is a matter for the LDS provider.
promises.summary: Clarify appropriate timing for formal mental health assessments by LDS providers

promises.quote: National guidelines are in place in the form of PACE Code C in relation to identifying vulnerability in police custody and the provision of an Appropriate Adult. It is not clear from the information in the report as to why the interviewing officer did not deem the support of an Appropriate Adult for Mr Hurley necessary in this case.
promises.summary: Ensure compliance with PACE Code C for Appropriate Adult provision
